E1.title: Prefetch Degree Sensitivity (k = 1 to 5)
E1.what_tested: Evaluated prefetch degrees k = 1, 2, 3, 5 with 1st-order Markov model on 1,024 RAM frames.
E1.what_found: Top-3 gave the largest saving of the degrees tested (15.04% fewer faults). Top-5 saved less (+6.88%); one possible cause is that extra low-probability pages displace resident ones, which we did not test.

table.notes: Pollution begins; 5,529 faults worse than Top-3

E2.title: 2nd-Order Markov Transition Model
E2.what_tested: Evaluated 2nd-order Markov model P(p_t | p_{t-1}, p_{t-2}) to test whether longer history improves prediction.
E2.what_found: Negative result: the 2nd-order model made more faults than baseline at k=2, 3 and 5 (up to 1.10% worse). Its table has 403,006 states against 2,025 for the 1st-order model. We did not test why it does worse; sparse statistics and thread interleaving are possible causes.

E3.title: RAM Capacity Sensitivity (512 to 2,048 Frames)
E3.what_tested: Evaluated Top-3 Markov prefetching across memory constraints: 512 frames (2 MB), 1,024 frames (4 MB), 2,048 frames (8 MB).
E3.what_found: At 512 frames, prefetching caused severe pollution and made faults 7.26% worse (221,603 -> 237,684). At 2,048 frames, abundant headroom yielded a 53.83% fault reduction (2,025 -> 935).

E4.title: Confidence Threshold Filtering
E4.what_tested: Filtered speculative prefetch candidates by transition probability threshold T in [0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50].
E4.what_found: Filtering low-probability tail transitions at T=0.10 yielded peak fault reduction (+17.65%, 55,751 faults), saving 1,761 more faults than unconditional Top-3 while issuing 7,382 fewer prefetches.

E5.title: Prefetch-Aware LRU Insertion (LRU-End Insertion)
E5.what_tested: Evaluated inserting prefetched speculative pages at the LRU position instead of the MRU position under memory pressure.
E5.what_found: Turned the 512-frame loss of -7.26% (237,684 faults) into +13.54% (191,587 faults), saving 46,097 faults compared with MRU insertion. The gain mixes two effects that were not separated: prefetched pages go to the LRU end, and predicted pages that are already resident are not moved to the MRU end.

E6.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Top-K Controller
E6.what_tested: Evaluated online dynamic adjustment of k every 1,000 faults based on interval precision and waste.
E6.what_found: Autonomous memory protection: at 512 frames, detected high waste (>0.50) and throttled k down to 2 (159 adjustments), turning -7.26% loss into +4.29% reduction (212,106 faults). At 1,024 frames, expanded k to 5 (57,609 faults, +14.90%).

E7.title: Adaptive Replacement Cache (ARC) vs LRU Baseline
E7.what_tested: Evaluated Megiddo & Modha's Adaptive Replacement Cache (ARC) with frequency + recency ghost lists against standard LRU without prefetching.
E7.what_found: ARC gave no gain over LRU (-0.36% at 512 frames, -0.01% at 1,024, 0.00% at 2,048). Its target parameter p stayed at 0, so it behaved like LRU on this trace. We did not test why.

E8.title: Graph-Aware Topological Oracle vs Statistical Markov
E8.what_tested: Compared statistical Markov prefetching against a Graph Oracle that prefetches direct graph neighbors from the CSR adjacency matrix.
E8.what_found: The graph oracle reached 57,230 faults (+15.46%), 282 faults (0.42 points) fewer than the Markov table (57,512, +15.04%). The Markov saving of 10,184 faults is 97.3% of the oracle's saving of 10,466 faults. The oracle is built from the whole graph with page numbers copied from this trace's layout, so it is not independent and is a reference point, not a proven upper bound.

E9.title: Per-Thread Markov vs Global Markov
E9.what_tested: Evaluated per-thread Markov models (22 separate transition tables) to test whether separating thread interleaved streams reduces entropy.
E9.what_found: Negative result: Per-thread Top-3 (+12.44%, 58,650 faults) did worse than Global Top-3 (+14.13%, 57,512 faults). The per-thread tables hold 44,398 states against 2,025 for the global table. We did not test why the split model does worse; thinner transition counts and BFS frontiers shared across threads are possible causes.

E10.title: Page Size Sensitivity under Fixed 4 MB RAM
E10.what_tested: Evaluated impact of page granularity (2 KB, 4 KB, 8 KB, 16 KB) under fixed 4 MB physical RAM allocation.
E10.what_found: The reduction does not rise steadily with page size: +14.68% at 2 KB, +14.13% at 4 KB, +15.28% at 8 KB and +15.83% at 16 KB. The Markov table shrinks from 4,049 states at 2 KB to 511 at 16 KB. We did not test why 4 KB is the lowest.

E11.title: Write-Back Overhead & Total Eviction Cost
E11.what_tested: Charged total I/O cost = page faults + dirty page evictions to account for write-back disk penalties.
E11.what_found: Prefetching increased total frame evictions from 65,955 to 113,643 and dirty evictions from 1,871 to 2,620. Because demand faults fell by 9,467, the combined cost still improved by +12.66% (68,850 -> 60,132 cost units). This cost counts faults and dirty evictions but does not charge the prefetch reads. The gain disappears if one prefetch read costs more than about 0.15 of a demand-fault read (8,718 cost units saved / 57,155 prefetches issued = 0.1525).
